payload.body: A stereo technique (or stereophonic sound) is a method of sound reproduction that uses two or more independent audio channels to create a spatial perception of sound, simulating multi-directional positioning. The system encodes, transmits, or reproduces separate signals for distinct channels (typically left and right), and a playback system renders these through separate speakers positioned to exploit human binaural hearing — using interaural time differences, interaural level differences, and spectral filtering by the pinnae — to produce a convincing soundstage. Parameters: minimum two discrete channels; channel count may exceed two (surround, ambient noise control, spatial audio); persistence through standardization in recording, broadcasting, and consumer electronics infrastructure. payload.body: Spectral processing is the method of analyzing and manipulating signals in their frequency-domain representation. It operates by applying the Fourier transform (or variants like STFT, DCT, wavelet transforms) to decompose a time-domain waveform into its constituent frequency components, then applying operations (filtering, amplification, attenuation, phase manipulation) to those frequency bands before reconstructing a modified signal via inverse transform. Parameters: (1) the transform type (DFT, FFT, STFT, wavelet), (2) the window function for time-localized transforms, (3) the frequency resolution determined by transform size and sampling rate, (4) the specific manipulation applied to spectral components. Persistence mechanism: implemented in DSP algorithms, embedded in audio software (spectral editors, FFT analyzers, spectral plugins), taught in signal processing curricula. [formal: spectrale_proc | substrate: mind | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 1.00]

payload.body: Headphones are a human-made electroacoustic device comprising a pair of miniature loudspeakers (drivers) in earcups, or a single housing containing two drivers, mounted on a headband or ear hook and worn by one listener to convert an electrical audio signal into sound pressure delivered directly to the ears. Parameters: (1) transduction — dynamic, electrostatic, planar-magnetic, or bone-conductive drivers; (2) coupling — over-ear, on-ear, or in-ear seal controlling acoustic isolation; (3) channel configuration — mono or two independent channels (stereo); (4) connectivity — wired (3.5 mm jack, USB) or wireless (radio, Bluetooth); (5) form factor — circumaural, supra-aural, or intraural. The persistence mechanism is industrial: the form is designed, mass-manufactured, and sold through retail channels as a durable consumer product category; individual units die in replacement cycles, but the category persists through continuous production, interface standardization (jack sizes, radio protocols), and the consumer-ownership cycle that keeps the form in daily use across decades. [formal: auditubera | substrate: matter | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.15]

payload.body: A transducer is an engineered device that converts energy from one physical form to another through a defined transduction mechanism. Its parameters are: (1) an input domain specifying the source energy type (electrical, mechanical, thermal, optical, chemical, magnetic), (2) an output domain specifying the destination energy type, (3) a transduction principle governing the conversion (electromagnetic induction, piezoelectric effect, thermoelectric effect, photoelectric effect, electrostatic force), and (4) a linearity specification describing whether the output is proportional to the input. payload.body: A digital-to-analog-converter is an electronic circuit or integrated chip that reconstructs a continuous analog voltage waveform from a stream of discrete digital codes. Its parameters are: (1) resolution — the number of bits per sample, determining quantization precision (8-bit to 32-bit commonly); (2) sampling rate — the maximum rate at which new analog values are produced, measured in samples per second; (3) output format — unbuffered voltage, buffered voltage, or current output depending on downstream requirements; (4) reconstruction filter — analog low-pass filter removing spectral images above the Nyquist frequency; (5) reference voltage — the full-scale analog range mapped from the digital code range. Persistence mechanism: manufactured through semiconductor fabrication (CMOS, BiCMOS, or bipolar processes), distributed through electronics supply chains, maintained through firmware updates (for programmable DACs) or physical replacement. payload.body: An analog-to-digital converter (ADC) is a hardware device that converts a continuous-time analog signal into a discrete-time, discrete-amplitude digital representation. Parameters: sampling rate (samples per second, determining the maximum reconstructible frequency via the Nyquist criterion), bit depth (number of quantization levels, 2^n, determining signal-to-quantization-noise ratio), and anti-aliasing filter bandwidth (low-pass filter before sampling). The device operates via three stages: (1) anti-aliasing filtering to band-limit the input, (2) sampling via a track-and-hold circuit, and (3) quantization and encoding via an ADC architecture (successive-approximation register, flash, sigma-delta, or pipelined). The persistence mechanism is electronic circuitry — silicon-integrated ADC chips or discrete components — that continuously maps instantaneous analog voltage to binary codes. The output is a stream of digital words representing the input waveform at each sampling instant. Law 8 removal test fails at the core of the operation. Stereo's accepted definition: a method of sound reproduction using two or more independent channels to create spatial perception, which 'encodes, transmits, or reproduces separate signals.' The technique's operation — capturing or playing back two independent channels — is recording and reproduction, not modifying, analyzing, or combining signals (audio-processing's carve). Remove audio-processing and stereo still operates: a binaural two-microphone recording with no processing of any kind still produces stereo playback and spatial perception, because the spatial image comes from the independent channels plus the listener's binaural hearing, not from processing. Only stereo's enhancements (panning, matrix encoding, spatialization) are processing operations — partial use of audio-processing, which is not the whole operation ceasing. Note: if any edge were warranted it would be that panning/spatialization (the processing sub-operations) relate to audio-processing, not that the reproduction technique depends on it.

Law 8d 'for whose sake?' fails against the target's own accepted definition. The DAC's accepted definition and scope carve a domain-agnostic circuit: it 'reconstructs a continuous analog voltage waveform from a stream of discrete digital codes', persisting 'as the standard bridge between digital sources and analog amplification in audio, video, and control practice' — three masters, not one. Its designed purpose is signal-domain conversion; audio playback is one of many application domains alongside video, telecom, test-and-measure, and control. 8d requires the purpose to be by design or sustained practice, 'not incidental benefit' — audio engineering is an application, not the design object, of the general-purpose circuit. Compare the mic/monitoring precedents that ADV: those devices exist for audio capture/monitoring as their sole domain. A generic DAC is not built for the sake of audio-engineering; 'for the sake of analog signal generation in general' would be the honest statement, and no such entry is the master here. The pinned sense attributes an audio-specific design purpose the accepted definition does not carry.

The removal test fails against the target's accepted definition — audio-processing is a MAP of operations (amplification, filtering, mixing, effects, spatialization, analysis), and stereo's accepted definition locates its mechanism in channel independence plus BINAURAL PSYCHOACOUSTICS (interaural time/level differences, pinna filtering): a raw two-channel recording played through two speakers is full stereo with no processing operation at all. A technique does not DEPEND_ON an operations map (CONCEPT referent); the board's own accepted pattern is specific-operation INSTANCE_OF the map (mid-side-processing, audio-routing) and technique DEPENDS_ON its operand (stereo->signal, ACCEPTED).

Signal-chain is defined as a human-made conceptual model in audio engineering that represents an audio signal's route as an ordered sequence of processing stages. Its parameters are stage list, topology, boundary signal state, insertion point, and its persistence mechanism is audio-engineering practice — routing diagrams, patch-bay wiring, DAW routing, console signal-flow teaching. The entry's scope justification explicitly names audio engineering. The note correctly pins servant→master: the model is built for describing studio and live setups within audio engineering. This matches the accepted pattern where conceptual tools for audio engineering serve audio engineering, e.g., audio monitoring→audio-engineering accepted.

Audio bus is defined as a human-made audio routing construct that aggregates multiple audio sources into a single channel for collective processing and mixing. Parameters include bus type, signal routing topology, processing chain, level summing. Persistence is through standard wiring conventions in analog consoles and routing objects in DAWs, documented in audio engineering literature and maintained through session templates. The entry's scope justification names audio routing construct built to persist as a channel for collective processing in studio practice. SERVES direction holds: the construct is built for audio engineering's mixing and bussing needs. Consistent with accepted audio monitoring→audio-engineering and microphone→audio-engineering.
